newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Losec boosts Astra to higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Losec boosts Astra to higher profits.

text.p: Swedish drugs group Astra AB on Monday posted an eight precent rise in pre-tax profit for the first nine months of 1996, boosted by sharp rise in sales of blockbusting ulcer drug Losec.
Sales rose just five percent to 28.14 billion crowns, but Astra said the stronger crown had made comparisons with 1995 less flattering.
"Calculated at constant exchange rates, sales growth was 16 percent which is the same growth as in the first half of the year," Astra said in its nine month report.
Pre-tax profit rose to 9.85 billion crowns in the nine months ending September 30.
Astra said worldwide sales of its leading drug, the antipeptic ulcer agent Losec, increased to 17.78 billion crowns ($2.7 billion) compared to 15.55 billion a year earlier.
This included all sales in the U.S., where Astra markets Losec in conjunction with Merck Inc through joint venture vehicle Astra Merck with the drug called Prilosec.
Astra's share of Losec sales rose 12 percent to 12.74 billion crowns -- or 22 percent at constant exchange rates.
Sales of its second largest drug, the anti-asthma agent Pulmicort, edged up three percent to 3.32 billion crowns.

Astra said its beta-blocker Seloken, which is its largest product in the cardiovascular group, was showing rapid growth, rising four percent to 1.87 billion crowns, or 17 percent at constant exchange rates.
"This was mainly due to a favourable trend in the U.S. where the product has been marketed since 1992 under the name Toprol-XL," the company said.
Sales in the pain control group rose three percent at constant exchange rates to 2.40 billion crowns.
The result was in line with market expectations. A Reuter poll found a market consensus forecast for a pre-tax profit of 9.81 billion crowns.
Astra opened slightly lower on the Stockholm bourse, slipping two crowns to 300 crowns in the first five minutes of trade.
